reason: The text describes divine judgment and plagues sent by God in response to Pharaoh's refusal to obey God's command to release the Israelites. While the text contains descriptions of destructive plagues, these are explicitly framed as God's acts of judgment (שְׁפָטִים - 'judgments') and demonstrations of divine power (לְמַעַן תֵּדַע כִּי אֲנִי יְהוָה - 'so that you know that I am the Lord'), not as a model for human leadership. Moses is presented as a faithful intermediary who follows God's instructions, not as a leader using violence to manage 'unruly people.' The leadership model portrayed involves obedience to God and faithfully carrying out His commands, not employing violence as a governance strategy.
